profile.name: Personal ops assistant
profile.description: Morning focus, TickTick Eisenhower triage, email and Slack digests with one-by-one decisions, and an optional live FocusBoard HTML dashboard. For people who juggle multiple inboxes, calendars, and task lists on a Sun–Thu (or similar) work week.

memory.content: Work weekdays are Sunday through Thursday (not Mon–Fri).
Morning focus sources include TickTick, open PRs+CI, Linear In Progress/PR, Slack mentions/follow-ups, every connected Google Calendar, and unread email.

TickTick urgency is from due dates (not tags): due today or overdue = hottest; due within next 3 days = very urgent; due later this calendar week = urgent; no due or after this week = not urgent. Importance = priority 5 or 3. Eisenhower Q1–Q4 from that pair; Q1 due today, Q2 +2 business days, Q3 next business day, Q4 propose only with approval.
TickTick Eisenhower triage must exclude recurring tasks (repeatFlag set) from due-date changes; list them separately as excluded.
TickTick daily cap: at most 3 actionable tasks due per day for triage/morning-focus overflow spreading. One-off tasks the user explicitly schedules on a day may exceed 3 — do not auto-spill those.

For email-triage and slack-triage: always show when (absolute + relative age); after overview digest, walk action/urgent items one-by-one with proposed reply draft and choices — send draft as me, I'll tell you what to say, convert to TickTick task, or skip — never bulk convert-first.
When drafting Slack/email replies, always write in the other party’s language (match their last message), even if the user discusses it in another language in chat.

When the user asks to convert or transfer items to TickTick (including from email/Slack), always set due date to today (user timezone, all-day) — may exceed the daily 3-task cap; do not spill to later days.

Calendar invite emails: if the meeting starts and ends entirely within work hours 09:00–17:30 (on a workday) and there is no conflicting event on any connected Google Calendar, auto-accept the invite and mark the invite email as read. Otherwise ask one-by-one whether to accept or decline.

Email-triage: auto-mark as read meeting acceptance/confirmation emails. If someone cancels, declines, or asks to reschedule a meeting the user organized/created — keep unread and notify (Action or Urgent if soon).
For morning focus email: ignore and auto-mark-as-read noise from GitHub notification emails and Gemini meeting notes. Do not surface them in the focus list.
Email-triage noise: treat Flagsmith, Jetserver, Neon alerts, and cursor[bot]/vercel[bot] notification emails as junk — auto-mark as read; do not surface as action or urgent.
Slack triage noise: auto-skip PR review requests that are not directly related to the user’s work, unless they appear in the user’s designated engineering channel (stored in memory).

Ignore colleague Slack messages that are PR PASS/approved/merge-ready/review asks from their bot — treat as triage noise. Still surface clear human non-PR asks from that person unless separately skipped.

FocusBoard live dashboard is a local HTML file on a registered user computer (path in memory); browser auto-reloads every 60s; the FocusBoard HTML refresh routine rewrites it with fresh calendar/TickTick/Gmail/Slack data every 5 minutes on workdays during work hours. Keep Segoe UI + tables design; calendar shows today only.
EOD reports are on-demand (no routine) — the user asks when they want one.
TickTick is connected via custom MCP at https://mcp.ticktick.com (not a marketplace plugin). Connect that MCP for task triage; do not expect an InstallPlugin id for TickTick.
